It indicates the multitude of those who will be called, as it is large and countless. For your sons, whom you have lost, will say into your ears, 'Make room for me.' It has been said somewhere also to the intelligible Zion, 'Enlarge the place of your tent and stretch out the curtains of your dwellings. Do not spare, but extend to the right and to the left.' We have read also in the books of Moses that around the tent in the wilderness, which was made through the hands of the skilled workers, wide and spacious curtains were placed, some facing east and the rising sun, others behind the tent to the west, and also to the north and south, indicating the future breadth and length of the holy courts, or the churches. However, even though the grace from Christ is always abundant, the places are narrow for those who believe, so that the Church, which is the intelligible Zion, rejoices and says to itself, 'Who has borne these for me?' I would say that it is faith in Christ. For through it, though you were childless and a widow, you have become numerous in children; this faith has nourished your people for you, and you, who were once seized and alone, have been unexpectedly clothed and have appeared with many children, you who were once naked and alone. Thus says the Lord, 'Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my signal to the islands, and they will bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters on their shoulders. And kings will be your nurses, and queens your wet nurses; they will bow down to you and lick the dust of your feet.'

And you will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be ashamed or embarrassed. Having promised to Zion that she will be many-childed and fertile, and that her children will come to her, so that she will need wider places and will be urged to expand her tent, it shows that the multitude of promised children to her is not from Israel, but from the multitude of the nations. Truly, the thing is, and through them the things are seen. For the remnant of Israel will be saved, but this is small and few in number. The power of the apostolic and evangelical preachings has brought to him the ones from all over the world through faith in Christ. That this will be, it shows by saying: Behold, I raise my hand to the nations. The 'raise' means to lift up and exalt. The hand signifies power or strength. When Christ was made known to the nations through the evangelical preachings, he became high and renowned through the wonders he worked, and through the resurrection…
pass_b_english: The multitude of those who will be called is indeed large and countless, indicating the vast number of people who will be part of the Church.
The sons who were lost will say to their mother, 'Make room for me,' as they return to her.

This is also said to the intelligible Zion, which is the Church, 'Enlarge the place of your tent and stretch out the curtains of your dwellings. Do not spare, but extend to the right and to the left' (Isaiah 54:2).

We read in the books of Moses that the tent in the wilderness had wide and spacious curtains, which were made through the hands of the skilled workers, some facing east and the rising sun, others behind the tent to the west, and also to the north and south, indicating the future breadth and length of the holy courts, or the churches.

However, even though the grace from Christ is always abundant, the places are narrow for those who believe, so that the Church, which is the intelligible Zion, rejoices and says to itself, 'Who has borne these for me?'
I would say that it is faith in Christ, through which the Church, though once childless and a widow, has become numerous in children.
Faith has nourished the people, and the Church, once seized and alone, has been unexpectedly clothed and has appeared with many children, who were once naked and alone.

Thus says the Lord, 'Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my signal to the islands, and they will bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters on their shoulders. And kings will be your nurses, and queens your wet nurses; they will bow down to you and lick the dust of your feet' (Isaiah 49:22-23).
You will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be ashamed or embarrassed.

Having promised to Zion that she will be many-childed and fertile, and that her children will come to her, so that she will need wider places and will be urged to expand her tent, it is true that the multitude of promised children to her is not from Israel, but from the multitude of the nations, and through them, the things are seen.
When Christ was made known to the nations through the evangelical preachings, he became high and renowned through the wonders he worked, and through the resurrection.
The hand indeed signifies the strength, that is the power, when the Lord says 'I will lift up my hand' it means to lift up and exalt.
The power of the apostolic and evangelical preachings has brought to him the ones from all over the world through faith in Christ.
The remnant of Israel will be saved, but this is a small and limited number.
